arxiv-2006-07677.title: Total Chromatic Number for Some Classes of Cayley Graphs
arxiv-2006-07677.creator: S. Prajnanaswaroopa, J. Geetha, K. Somasundaram
arxiv-2006-07677.description: Abstract Abstract: The Total coloring conjecture states that any simple graph G with maximum degree \Delta can be totally colored with at most \Delta+2 colors. In this paper, we have obtained the total chromatic number for some classes of Cayley graphs. Keywords: Cayley graphs; Total coloring; Circulant graphs; Perfect Cayley graphs.

arxiv-2011-14291.title: Erasure-Resilient Sublinear-Time Graph Algorithms
arxiv-2011-14291.creator: Amit Levi, Ramesh Krishnan S. Pallavoor, Sofya Raskhodnikova, Nithin Varma
arxiv-2011-14291.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Amit Levi, Ramesh Krishnan S. Pallavoor, Sofya Raskhodnikova, Nithin Varma. We investigate sublinear-time algorithms that take partially erased graphs represented by adjacency lists as input. Our algorithms make degree and neighbor queries to the input graph and work with a specified fraction of adversarial erasures in adjacency entries. We focus on two computational tasks: testing if a graph is connected or ε \varepsilon -far from connected and estimating the average degree.

arxiv-2208-11843.title: Comparing Storm Resolving Models and Climates via Unsupervised Machine Learning DOI: www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.XXXXXXXXXX
arxiv-2208-11843.creator: Griffin Mooers, Mike Pritchard, Tom Beucler, Prakhar Srivastava, Harshini Mangipudi, Liran Peng, Pierre Gentine, Stephan Mandt
arxiv-2208-11843.description: Abstract \nolinenumbers Global Storm-Resolving Models (GSRMs) have gained widespread interest because of the unprecedented detail with which they resolve the global climate. However, it remains difficult to quantify objective differences in how GSRMs resolve complex atmospheric formations. This lack of comprehensive tools for comparing model similarities is a problem in many disparate fields that involve simulation tools for complex data.

arxiv-2302-13129.title: Axion electrodynamics: Green’s functions, zero-point energy and optical activity
arxiv-2302-13129.creator: Amedeo M. Favitta, Iver H. Brevik, Moshe M. Chaichian
arxiv-2302-13129.description: Abstract Starting from the theory of Axion Electrodynamics, we work out the axionic modifications to the electromagnetic Casimir energy using the Green’s function method, both when the axion field is initially assumed purely time-dependent and when the axion field configuration is a static domain wall, so purely space-dependent.

arxiv-2408-16541.title: Causal Mechanisms of Subpolar Gyre Variability in CMIP6 Models
arxiv-2408-16541.creator: Swinda K.J. Falkena, Henk A. Dijkstra, Anna S. von der Heydt
arxiv-2408-16541.description: Abstract The subpolar gyre is at risk of crossing a tipping point under future climate change associated with the collapse of deep convection. As such tipping can have significant climate impacts, it is important to understand the mechanisms at play and how they are represented in modern climate models.

arxiv-2505-21316.title: Efficient Leaf Disease Classification and Segmentation using Midpoint Normalization Technique and Attention Mechanism
arxiv-2505-21316.creator: Enam Ahmed Taufik, Antara Firoz Parsa, Seraj Al Mahmud Mostafa
arxiv-2505-21316.description: Abstract Enhancing plant disease detection from leaf imagery remains a persistent challenge due to scarce labeled data and complex contextual factors. We introduce a transformative two-stage methodology: Mid Point Normalization (MPN) for intelligent image preprocessing, coupled with sophisticated attention mechanisms that dynamically recalibrate feature representations.

arxiv-2506-01902.title: Enhancing Biomedical Multi-modal Representation Learning with Multi-scale Pre-training and Perturbed Report Discrimination
arxiv-2506-01902.creator: Xinliu Zhong, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Li Sun
arxiv-2506-01902.description: Abstract Vision-language models pre-trained on large scale of unlabeled biomedical images and associated reports learn generalizable semantic representations. These multi-modal representations can benefit various downstream tasks in the biomedical domain. Contrastive learning is widely used to pre-train vision-language models for general natural images and associated captions.

pmc-11458685.title: Secondary vertex reconstruction with MaskFormers
pmc-11458685.creator: Samuel Van Stroud, Nikita Pond, Max Hart, Jackson Barr, Sébastien Rettie, Gabriel Facini, Timothy Scanlon
pmc-11458685.description: In high-energy particle collisions, the reconstruction of secondary vertices from heavy-flavour hadron decays is crucial for identifying and studying jets initiated by b- or c-quarks. Traditional methods, while effective, require extensive manual optimisation and struggle to perform consistently across wide regions of phase space.

pmc-11484965.title: Exploring neural markers of dereification in meditation based on EEG and personalized models of electrophysiological brain states
pmc-11484965.creator: Tamas Madl
pmc-11484965.description: With mounting evidence for the benefits of meditation, there has been a growing interest in measuring and quantifying meditative states. This study introduces the Inner Dereification Index (IDI), a class of personalized models designed to quantify the distance from non-meditative states such as mind wandering based on a single individual’s neural activity.

pmc-11738387.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Their Association With Neurodegenerative Disorders: A Systematic Narrative Review
pmc-11738387.creator: Rebecca Restorick, Huw Dunstall, Katja Umla-Runge
pmc-11738387.description: AimsNeurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), such as dyslexia, dyspraxia, and dyscalculia affect cognitive function and therefore share symptomology with neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease, vascular dementia, and frontotemporal lobe dementia. The primary aim of this narrative systematic review is to ascertain if there is an association between NDDs and neurodegenerative disorders.

pmc-12452529.title: Self-Perceived Health Status and Life Satisfaction Associated with Emotional Eating in Nursing and Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Study in a Region of Peru
pmc-12452529.creator: Jacksaint Saintila, Ana Valle-Chafloque, Luz A. Barreto-Espinoza, Elmer López-López, Norma Del Carmen Gálvez-Díaz, Isabel G. Lizarraga-De-Maguiña, Noemi Alejandrina Buenaño Cervera, Susan M. Oblitas-Guerrero, Fátima del Carmen Bernal-Corrales, Giovanna Larraín Távara
pmc-12452529.description: Background: Emotional eating (EmE) is a maladaptive eating behavior that has been frequently observed among university students, possibly due to academic stress and lifestyle changes. However, its specific assessment in health science students has been poorly addressed, even though this population faces high levels of academic stress and emotional burden.

pmc-12457636.title: Lineage-specific targets of positive selection in three leaf beetles correspond with defence capacity against their shared parasitoid wasp
pmc-12457636.creator: Xuyue Yang, Kalle Tunström, Tanja Slotte, Christopher W. Wheat, Peter A. Hambäck
pmc-12457636.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Parasitoid wasps are major causes of mortality of many species, making host immune defences a common target of adaptive evolution, though such targets outside model species are poorly understood. In this study, we used two tests of positive selection to compare across three closely related Galerucella leaf beetles that show substantial differences in their phenotypic response to the shared parasitoid wasp Asecodes parviclava, their main natural enemy.

pmc-12504370.title: Diffuse midline glioma with extra central nervous system metastases in the pediatric, adolescent, and young adult population
pmc-12504370.creator: Alexandra M. Giantini-Larsen, Andrew L. A. Garton, Maricruz Rivera, Rachael Han, David J. Pisapia, Sameer Farouk Sait, Matthias A. Karajannis, Jeffrey P. Greenfield, Mark H. Bilsky, W. Christopher Newman, Mark M. Souweidane
pmc-12504370.description: Diffuse midline gliomas (DMG) are malignant infiltrative gliomas enriched in the pediatric population and characterized by loss of the H3 K27me3 epigenetic marker, most frequently via mutation of the H3-3A gene. Few cases of extra-central nervous system (CNS) DMG metastasis with redemonstrated H3-3A p.K28M (H3K27M) mutation in metastatic tissue are reported in the literature.

pmc-12731758.title: Targeting MARylation and DePARylation in Cancer Therapy: New Promising Therapeutic Opportunities
pmc-12731758.creator: Vanesa Cabeza-Fernández, Francisco Javier Ríos-Sola, David Martín-Oliva, Jerónimo Borrego-Pérez, Francisco Javier Oliver, José YéLamos, José Manuel Rodríguez-Vargas, Dik C van Gent
pmc-12731758.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryADP-ribosylation is a post-translational modification that plays a crucial role in DNA repair, transcription, replication, and overall cell fitness. The ADP-ribose cycle represents one of the most tightly regulated biochemical pathways in the cell, as precise control of mono- and poly-ADP-ribose levels, together with the coordinated activity of the enzymes that synthesize and recycle ADP-ribose to NAD+, is essential for cellular homeostasis.

pmc-13150370.title: From separate streams to confluence: A framework for meaningful mixed methods integration in African primary care research
pmc-13150370.creator: Robin E. Dyers, Kéfilath Bello, Timothy C. Guetterman
pmc-13150370.description: Mixed methods research is becoming more common in African primary care studies, yet systematic reviews show most mixed methods studies demonstrate low methodological rigour in integrating qualitative and quantitative components. This integration failure undermines addressing complex health challenges facing African primary care systems, where medical pluralism, resource constraints, and diverse disease burdens demand sophisticated methodological synthesis.

pmc-13590011.title: Trichinella detection in wild boar meat intended for private consumption: Insights from a European study
pmc-13590011.creator: Mariana Rodrigues, Edoardo Pozio, Vincenzo Veneziano, Famke Jansen, Thomai Lazou, Sorin Daniel Dan, Miroslaw Różycki, Jelena Petrović, Madalena Vieira-Pinto
pmc-13590011.description: Private consumption of wild boar meat is increasingly widespread across Europe. Notably, only a small proportion of hunted game is processed through approved establishments, while the majority is intended for private consumption. Testing wild boar meat for Trichinella spp. is mandatory when the meat is placed on the market.
